finally, any inaccuracies are entirely my own. i hope you enjoy!

It is a typical sunny day in the Marmoreal Diner when Phainon corners Caelus. What is not so typical (or maybe it is, because Caelus has done a lot of strange things in the Diner) is that Phainon finds Caelus as he’s wailing into his cup, while the other customers look on awkwardly.

“May I sit here?” Phainon asks him. Caelus nods, miserable, and watches as Phainon takes the seat across from him.

Phainon makes a sympathetic face. “What happened? Are you alright?”

Caelus shows him his phone screen. “My favourite character just died,” he bawls.

“I’m sorry to hear that,” Phainon says. He reaches out, and pats Caelus on the shoulder.

Caelus takes the opportunity to bawl louder. The customer on their right visibly flinches.

“I spent hours grinding for his levels,” Caelus wails. He swipes a hand across his eyes, and dries his tears. “He was beautiful to me.”

Phainon, still solemn, blinks at him. Do they even have games on their teleslates in Amphoreus, Caelus despairs. If not, the citizens are missing out, but it would explain why Phainon’s looking at him like he’s grown a second head. As if crying about a dead character was stupid.

Caelus opens his mouth to ask exactly that, but Phainon is already moving on.

“Speaking of beautiful men,” Phainon says smoothly, before winking—read the room, Caelus thinks indignantly, my favourite character just DIED!!!— “I actually came here to ask you a few questions, if you’d be happy to answer them.” He pauses, and scrutinises Caelus. He’s probably looking at the tear tracks still fresh on his cheeks. “Of course, if now isn’t a good time, I can always return later.”

Caelus waves him off. “It’s fine,” he sniffs. Then, he pauses. “Wait. What do you mean by ‘beautiful men’?”

Phainon laughs. “Exactly that. You see, I wanted to ask you about Dan Heng.” He leans forward in his chair, and interlocks his fingers. The motion makes him look like some sort of —mafia boss. “You mentioned that he had a previous lover?”

The gears going ballistic in Caelus’ head grind to a halt. He blanks.

Had he mentioned that?

Phainon gives him an encouraging nod. Caelus glances down at the table, and nearly startles when he realises that Phainon’s whipped out a golden pen. Said pen is poised over a pad of paper, evidently ready to scribble.

He looks up. The twinkle in Phainon’s eye is kind of scary.

“I think Dan Heng’s been married before,” Caelus offers slowly, “but it—” wasn’t really him? It was his past incarnation who just so happened to look like him? He has no idea how to explain Dan Heng’s long, confusing history.

Whatever. He can simplify it. Probably.

“His husband died,” Caelus decides. “And then Dan Heng died,” sorry, Dan Heng, but Phainon won’t get it otherwise, “but then he came back, and his husband also came back, and now that husband is his ex and used to spend his time hunting Dan Heng down. Dan Heng killed him once or twice, but it never works because he’s basically immortal. Like Mydei, but less polite and more murderous.”

The sound of furious scribbling pauses. Caelus chances a glance at Phainon, only to find him staring back at Caelus—politely, because it’s Phainon, but also like he’s actually grown a second head this time.

Caelus winces. “... It’s difficult to explain?”

“I… see.” Phainon clearly does not see, but thankfully, he doesn’t press. And as amazingly perceptive as Caelus is, he really has no clue how to explain Vidyadharan rebirth. “And is this ex-husband… out of the picture?”

Caelus scratches his nose. “Er,” he says intelligently, thinking back to the last time they saw Blade. “We do see him from time to time? He doesn’t really talk to us, though. I tried texting him once and he left me on read.”

“He doesn’t pursue Dan Heng?” Phainon presses, oddly intent. “They aren’t together?”

“He’s pretty obsessive…” Caelus frowns. “But he was calmer the last time I saw him. We try to keep them apart when we can. I don’t think they’re together.” Unless Dan Heng has been keeping a secret of epic proportions from everyone, that is.

At that, Phainon relaxes. He seems pleased. “Perfect! Are there any other contenders I should know about?”

“Contenders?” Like other lovers? Caelus furrows his brow. For some reason, he feels a sense of unease pool in his gut, like some sort of parasite wiggling about. “Well, there is this… general, and potentially a space cowboy, but to be honest, I think they’re just friends.”

“I see,” Phainon hums. He taps the pen against his bottom lip, looking very considerate and thoughtful. Caelus innocently peers over to look at his paper, but Phainon swiftly hides it from view, cheerful smile still on his face. Damn.

“That’s helpful,” Phainon continues. “Would you be able to tell me a little more about this general?”

“Sure,” says Caelus. He’s always up for glazing Jing Yuan, even if he has no idea why Phainon is asking.

Caelus shifts in his seat, and thinks. “Er—there’s a lot to say about him. He’s very strong. He can hold an eight-tonne guandao in one hand.” Caelus holds up his hands, and spreads them apart in an approximate estimate of Starfall Reverie’s size. “He loves animals, and he’s very gentle with them. I heard that he used to have a pet lion.”

“A pet lion? Interesting,” mutters Phainon, scribbling furiously even as he doesn’t break eye contact. The way those baby blue eyes bore into Caelus is kind of uncanny. “Anything else?”

Caelus shrugs helplessly. “Uh… Birds flock to him? As well as all the women. And the men.” He wracks his brain. “I heard he’s been the Most Eligible Bachelor on the Luofu for nearly 700 years running. And all his photocards keep selling out.”

Phainon’s pen has not left the paper in the entire time Caelus has spoken. It’s honestly impressive. Caelus thinks Phainon would make a great journalist, if he wasn’t a Deliverer.

Partly to give himself some reprieve, Caelus takes out his phone and navigates to his photo gallery. He tilts his screen in Phainon’s direction.

It’s a photo of Jing Yuan, napping serenely, with a finch nestled in his hair. Phainon gives it a passing glance, expression unchanging.

“Hmm,” is all he has to say.

Caelus blinks. Usually that picture gets a blush, even by decidedly unsingle men. Maybe Phainon is simply too loyal, in which case, good for him for escaping the allure of the esteemed General, he who unwittingly tempts even the most monogamous of men (not on purpose, is Caelus’ understanding, but the point still stands).

Phainon presses on. “And is this general—in a relationship?”

Caelus stretches his legs. He thinks to himself: can he describe the historical love triangle-slash-threesome that Jing Yuan had going on with his old friends? And comes to the conclusion that no, he probably can’t.

“Not that I know of?” Caelus answers instead. “Everyone wants him, but he’s kind of a… single father, with the aura of… a mourning widow?”

Phainon gives him a look of confusion. Come on, Caelus wants to wail, you’d agree with me if you saw him!

“A mourning widow full of whimsy,” is the descriptor that Caelus finally decides on. “Which I think actually adds to his appeal.” He thinks back to the numerous photocards that he’s seen, and the way the General had been portrayed on them. Enduring, gentle and world-weary—a perfect combination of traits that cater to literally everyone. “You could describe him as a MILF, I guess?”

Phainon cocks his head. “A MILF?”

In Caelus’ mind, an image of Dan Heng looming over him threateningly crystallises frighteningly fast.

“It’s nothing,” Caelus says hastily.

Thankfully, Phainon chooses to let it go. He stares at his paper and mutters under his breath instead, looking dissatisfied. “And what about this… ‘cow boy’?”

“He’s… eccentric,” Caelus answers, after some deliberation. “But funny. He’s a good guy, even if he likes to jump the gun a lot. Literally.”

“Hmm,” Phainon says. He scribbles harder, face scrunched up into an expression of absolute concentration. Caelus tries to read his writing upside down again, until he realises that Phainon is scrawling so quickly that his notes are all illegible shorthand. “And you’re sure there’s no one else?”

“Not that I know of,” Caelus says, slowly. The unease in his gut tugs again, insistent. “Why do you want to know all this?”

“Don’t worry about it,” Phainon says gravely. He tucks his papers away, looking immensely pleased with himself. Confused, Caelus can only watch on as Phainon rises to his feet.

“One last thing,” Phainon says brightly. “Do you have a spare board lying around?”

“A whiteboard? No,” Caelus answers, shaking his head. “Dan Heng broke my only one.”

“Worth a try,” Phainon smiles at him. He gives Caelus a jaunty wave. “I’ll see you later, my friend.”

With that, he’s out—a flash of gold, white and royal blue hurrying around the corner with a skip in his step. Caelus stares after him, wondering just what the hell he had been subjected to.

Most of Phainon’s words had sounded vaguely… ominous. Caelus prides himself on knowing Dan Heng’s juicy secrets so that he can pretend to use them as leverage over other people, but they’re all random useless Dan Heng facts (see example: inside behind-the-scenes anecdotes about his misshapen knitting attempts) rather than anything actually important. He doesn’t actually know about Dan Heng’s romantic past, other than the details the man has explicitly told him—which is basically nothing.

Phainon had been weirdly interested in Dan Heng’s dating history. And Caelus, for the life of him, can’t think of a reason why. Apart from the obvious conclusion.

Which isn’t actually that obvious, because—well.

Caelus frowns. He swipes back to his game, and unpauses the screen. His favourite character is still lying in the rainy field, where he’s just been pelted with bullets, and his friend is crying over him. Caelus’ eyes twitch, and so does his gut.

His favourite character gives his sword and legacy to his friend, and says some touching parting words before he dies. His friend screams, bone-chilling, and then the credits roll, and Caelus, through his welling tears, tries not to think about his conversation with Phainon.

Caelus keeps thinking about his conversation with Phainon.

It just doesn’t make sense. Why would Phainon suddenly ask him about Dan Heng’s exes? To Caelus’ knowledge, Phainon has never shown so much interest in Dan Heng before, so for him to suddenly raise so many questions is baffling.

After an hour of furious pondering, the only sensible conclusion Caelus comes up with is that Phainon could possibly want Dan Heng… carnally?

Is it because Dan Heng accidentally let slip some of his more draconian features, and Phainon was impressed? As much as Caelus hates to admit it, it kind of makes sense. After all, the first time that Caelus saw Dan Heng like that, his first thought had been something along the lines of ‘please step on me please please please’. It would be understandable if other people experienced the same emotion.

But the last time he checked, Phainon should be deeply in love with Mydei—not only because Caelus had quite literally risked his life trying to get the both of them together, but also because there really is no other explanation. The other day he’d found Phainon wearing Mydei’s earring, looking extraordinarily pleased with himself. Matching earrings are basically matching wedding rings in Caelus’ book—as are the letters he keeps seeing Phainon send, and the longing glances he sees Phainon direct towards the general direction of Castrum Kremnos, with enough yearning to fill even the most sappiest romance books, etcetera etcetera.

The point is that Phainon is a very happily taken man. As a happily taken man, why would he enquire about other men? Is that something that men do in Amphoreus?

Unfortunately, Caelus doesn’t get to think about it much, because for some reason, the door to his and Dan Heng’s room is stuck.

“I can’t believe that we’re actually stuck in our own room,” Caelus complains. He shoots off a quick SOS text to the Chrysos Heirs, and watches despairingly as no one responds.

“Hmm,” says Dan Heng, staring at the opposite wall.

“I mean, you would think we’d have trust issues after getting drugged in here,” Caelus rants. “Actually, I do have trust issues.”

“Mm.”

“Imagine they forgot about us here and we starved to death.” Caelus flops into a chair. He dramatically pretends to die. “Goodbye, Astral Express. Goodbye, March’s souvenirs.”

“Mmm.”

Caelus chances a quick glance at Dan Heng. He’s still staring at the far wall, but the crease in his brow is much more pronounced than Caelus would like.

Caelus swings his legs over the chair, and leans forward.

“Dan Heng, are you okay?” he asks seriously. “Are you feeling sick?”

“I’m fine,” Dan Heng says, far too quickly. “You shouldn’t worry about me.”

He can say that all he likes, but Caelus knows that look. Dan Heng is antsy, fingers twitching like he wants to fidget but he’s just about stopping himself. It’s the same way he looked the first time they visited the Luofu, back when he thought Caelus and March were busy getting skewered on the end of Blade’s, well, blade.

“You look down,” Caelus offers. “Want a hug?”

Dan Heng closes his eyes. When he speaks, he sounds pained. “No.”

Caeus opens his mouth to pester him again, but gets interrupted by a thump from the door.

He whirls around.  “Is someone there?” he calls hopefully. “Hello? We’re stuck— can you try and open the door from your side?”

The other side of the door is silent, even when Caelus rattles the doorknob and tugs it so hard he nearly breaks the thing. After struggling for a minute, and the lack of any response, he gives up. It was worth a try.

“Huh. Must have been the wind,” Caelus mutters. He turns around, and gives Dan Heng his signature thousand-watt smile. “Don’t worry, Dan Heng—I’ll get us out of here, no matter what. In the meantime…” now, he plasters on his most pathetic, pleading face, “are you sure you don’t want a hug?”

Dan Heng sighs. The crease in his brow softens, and his expression slips to one of fond, familiar exasperation.

That’s more like it, thinks Caelus happily.

“I’m truly fine, Caelus,” Dan Heng says, with the infinite patience of a long-suffering man. He pauses. “Please don’t jump on me.”

Caelus pouts, relaxing out of his stance. “Worth a try,” he sighs. Then, he retrieves his bat from its resting place next to his bed, and faces the door. “Well, then. Looks like we only have one solution left, huh?”

“Caelus,” Dan Heng launches forward, alarmed, “no, we’ve already been charged for property damage—”

So Caelus may have forgotten that Aglaea could deliver him a look that severe. Whoops! His fault.

In the process of getting stuck in their room for a day and collecting a second charge for property damage shortly afterwards, Caelus almost forgets about the whole Dan Heng and Phainon thing. Almost, until he happens to overhear (and definitely not eavesdrop on) a particular conversation later that day.

It’s not the sound of Phainon whining that clues him in, but rather, the sound of Phainon whining at Dan Heng, which is something that Caelus never thought he would see.

Caelus ducks behind a convenient pillar.

“—it was the perfect opportunity!” Phainon’s saying.

“It really wasn’t,” Dan Heng sighs. “The timing was terrible.”

“You have to make your intentions known—”

Caelus frowns. Intentions? What intentions?

Dan Heng crosses his arms. Caelus can’t make out his expression at this distance, but if he could hazard a guess, he would say that Dan Heng is probably looking exasperated again.

“Like you did?” Dan Heng asks.

The silence that follows is pointed.

“That was different!” Phainon protests. He sounds almost… embarrassed?

Dan Heng sighs again. “Thank you, Phainon, but I can’t just…”

Caelus holds his breath and tries to focus on their voices, but the pair are already walking away. His mind races. What ‘intentions’ does Dan Heng have? Does he have—a crush? The thought makes Caelus’ stomach twist, because the last time Dan Heng got into a relationship, his ex chased him across the entire universe.

Besides, he’s made a pact with March about this. If Dan Heng has a crush, then Caelus will definitely have to investigate for the both of them, because March would never let him live it down if she heard that he’d done nothing for their friend’s honour.

Caelus parks that troubling thought, and strains to listen to the last snatches of conversation before the pair disappear around the corner entirely.

“—spring this… out of nowhere,” Dan Heng’s saying. He sounds unhappy, now—almost frustrated.

Phainon earnestly lays a hand on Dan Heng’s shoulder. “Don’t worry,” he tells Dan Heng, and Caelus fights the urge to shiver. “Leave it to me.”

Phainon and Dan Heng were clearly discussing something important. But about what, Caelus thinks, more than a little disconcerted, and why is Dan Heng speaking to Phainon about it, and not me?

As it turns out, Phainon and Dan Heng keep discussing something important, because it seems that every time Caelus tries to catch Dan Heng, he’s talking with Phainon.

Take today, for example. Phainon’s talking to Dan Heng with so much excitement that he’s practically sparkling. Dan Heng responds with what Caelus can only describe as a groan. The tips of his ears are red.

Caelus feels stung. Since when did they get so close?

He doesn’t get time to ponder their relationship, because Phainon spots him easily. He elbows Dan Heng in the side, and points towards Caelus’ direction. His eyes are gleaming.

Dan Heng looks over. His eyes are decidedly not gleaming. He looks more like a deer caught in headlights.

“Would you look at that? I’m late for a meeting,” Phainon says, far too loudly. “I’ll talk to you both later!”

With that, Phainon disappears—quite literally—in a flash. Caelus will never understand how he does that.

He turns to Dan Heng. “What was that about?” Caelus asks, lost. “And what are you wearing?”

Dan Heng sighs, before slowly turning around. “Lady Aglaea felt compelled to make us new outfits that… better suit Okhema’s climate, as thanks for our aid to the Flamechase Journey,” he says, stiffly. “She made you a set, too. I’ve left it in our room.”

Caelus tries very hard not to stare.

Dan Heng’s wearing a sleeveless chiton that drapes artfully around his shoulders and legs. The teal accents match the jade of his eyes. He looks beautiful.

Not that he doesn’t always look beautiful. He just looks extra beautiful right now. Dreamy, even. Men would probably kill each other to see his ankles, and now look at him.

Despite his new fit, Dan Heng only scrunches in on himself, and looks away. The tips of his ears are still red, and his mouth is pursed unhappily.

Caelus frowns. It’s not like Dan Heng to be self-conscious. Maybe he’s cold? Or maybe the outfit shows too much skin? Dan Heng is usually more covered up, after all. His Imbibitor Lunae fit only really shows off his arms and that glorious back window, but Aglaea’s design leaves much more on display.

… Is Dan Heng uncomfortable?

A crowd of people have gathered behind them, tittering away with hushed whispers. Caelus usually pays their gossip no mind, but this time he only feels irritated. He steps forward, shielding Dan Heng from view, and shrugs out of his jacket.

“You’ll catch a cold,” Caelus scolds. Carefully, he drapes his jacket around Dan Heng’s shoulders, where goosebumps have already started studding his skin. “It’s not like you to forget your jacket, at least. You should be more careful.”

In the crowd, someone coughs. They sound almost incredulous.

Dan Heng sags with relief, and clutches the jacket around himself. He looks a bit ridiculous, but he definitely looks warmer. “You’re right; I will. Thank you, Caelus,” he says. Then, in a decidedly icier tone: “I should never have worn this in the first place.”

Caelus blinks. That sounded like it was directed at someone. But the crowd, easily bored, has already dispersed, and when he looks over, Dan Heng only seems to be glaring at… a barrel.

Eh, whatever. As long as Dan Heng’s feeling better, and no one’s laughing at him, Caelus won’t pay it too much attention.

“—didn’t think you’d be one to give up!”

Caelus, who actually didn’t mean to overhear this particular conversation, freezes in his tracks.

“Of course not, Hyacine, but don’t you think there’s an issue here if Mydei is having an easier job of this than I am? And he isn’t even in the city!” he hears Phainon groan. “Do you think that Dan Heng…”

Hyacine and Phainon’s voices trail off. Distantly, Caelus realises that there is undeniably something happening between Phainon and Dan Heng, that he can’t pass off as a coincidence now that even Hyacine is in on it.

Well! All this means is that he just has to snoop around and find out what the deal is. It shouldn’t be too difficult a job for Caelus, Mr Ace Detective. His sleuthing skills are the best in the universe, and once he’s on a case, he never gives up.

Caelus gives up.

“Dan Heng!” he shouts, slamming their door open. “Where are you? I need answers from you right… now…”

Inside the room, Dan Heng yelps—honest to Aeons yelps—and then whirls around, hands hidden behind his back.

“Caelus. Hello,” Dan Heng says, stiff as a board. “You’re back rather early.”

Caelus squints at Dan Heng, the same way he squints at March when she gets her hands on the cookie jar. Dan Heng only shuffles backwards in response, looking carefully neutral.

“Is that…”

“It’s nothing,” Dan Heng cuts him off, far too smoothly.

Caelus gasps, scandalised. “You’re hiding porn?”

At that, Dan Heng goes scarlet. “What—no—”

“Or what—adult literature? Doujinshi?” Caelus presses. He grins, enjoying the familiar glee that comes with teasing Dan Heng. “It’s a doujinshi, isn’t it? Dan Heng, you sly dog, did you sneak this onto the car with you—?”

Dan Heng’s face now looks hot enough to power several suns. Honestly, Caelus is worried that he’ll start to turn purple if he keeps going.

“It’s not a doujinshi—” Dan Heng hisses, practically steaming from his ears, “or—porn, or any other idea you’ve conjured in your mind—”

“Well, you’re hiding it like your life depends on it, so what else could it be apart from some —” Caelus consults his brain, and thinks of something that could make his dear friend pass out,  “—limited edition Jing Yuan playboy-esque boudoir bust-related—ow ow ow okay OKAY you can stop—!”

Dan Heng stops hitting him over the head. His red cheeks are adorable. “Please never refer to the General like that ever again.”

“You can’t deny it,” Caelus points out reasonably. “Anyway, there’s no need to be ashamed. I don’t think anyone in Amphoreus even knows what a doujinshi is.”

Dan Heng huffs. “Again, that’s not what it is,” he says pointedly, but looking less like a tomato and more like a Dan Heng, which Caelus supposes is a good thing. “But if you won’t be convinced… fine. Here.”

With what seems like great reluctance (and is that a whispered plea for mercy that Caelus hears?), Dan Heng hands Caelus the object he was hiding behind his back earlier, which happens to be… a piece of paper.

“What is it?” Caelus asks.

“I received a letter,” Dan Heng says. His tone is evasive.

Caelus peers down at the paper, hoping to get a sneak peek. Dan Heng, the party pooper, tilts the letter away from him, but he’s not quick enough to hide the sender’s name.

Caelus’ jaw drops, because that name is the last person he’d expect to be writing to Dan Heng.

“Happy now?” Dan Heng sighs, looking tired beyond his years.

“You’re writing to Mydei?” Caelus gapes. “Mydei?”

He knew that Mydei and Phainon had been communicating, but he assumed that was because they were a thing, now. He didn’t think Mydei would even have the time to write to anyone other than his new boyfriend. He also didn’t think Mydei and Dan Heng had that much in common that they’d be writing to each other like—penpals, or something.

Dan Heng shrugs. He looks very calm about this, Caelus notes, with some level of dull panic. “I only wanted to ask him a few questions. He’s just offering some advice.”

For some reason, his response just makes Caelus feel slightly ugly. “You’ve never written to me before,” he accuses.

At that, Dan Heng just presses a finger to his temple, looking like he’s nursing a headache. “That’s because we’ve always been together.”

That’s true, and it’s a comforting thought.

Still. Why would Mydei and Dan Heng write to each other while Mydei’s away fighting a one-man war?

Caelus is really having a problem, recently, regarding the amount of unwanted conversations he’s stumbling into. Especially when the number of unwanted conversations outnumbers the number of conversations he actually wants to eavesdrop on.

“He totally liked seeing you like that,” he hears Phainon tease, a few alleys away.

“I felt like a fool,” comes the disgruntled response.

From Dan Heng.

The words take a moment to register, but when they do, Caelus realises that he’s about two seconds away from passing out in the middle of the street.

Is Dan Heng sending pictures of himself? To Mydei? Pictures that Mydei liked?

And Phainon knows about it?

“We could put you in the baths?” Phainon muses, oblivious to Caelus nearly keeling over behind them.

“Please. No more of that,” Dan Heng mutters tiredly. “I don’t think it would be very effective. I’d also like to preserve my own dignity, if at all possible.”

Caelus’ legs go slack with shock, and nearly give out.

Is Dan Heng sending NUDES? Dan Heng?? Dan Heng???

For some reason, Phainon only sounds crestfallen. “I see you really are taking Mydei’s advice. When did he write to you last? He’s been ignoring me—probably because of our competition—and please don’t tell him this but I can’t believe that he’s winning when he’s not even present—”

ARE YOU AND MYDEI NOT TOGETHER??? Caelus wants to scream. WHAT THE HELL HAPPENED IN THE SPACE OF ONE WEEK???

He misses the rest of the conversation and honestly most of everything else after that, because Dan Heng and Phainon’s voices get closer, and thus Caelus is forced to run back to his room, feeling confused and also strangely like some sort of heartbroken maiden.

So apparently Dan Heng is with Mydei… with Phainon’s permission? Did Phainon and Mydei break up? There’s no way they’d break up—yet Caelus can’t think of any other alternative to describe what he’d just witnessed.

The prospect leaves a sour taste in Caelus’ mouth, and he gets the sudden urge to find the nearest wall and bash his head against it.

Caelus’ mood is terrible enough that even the prospect of gathering intel doesn’t thrill him the way it used to. He spends the next few days moping around Okhema and halfheartedly fulfilling people’s requests. Judging by the worried glances the citizens are giving him, he probably looks like some sort of listless ghost, dragging his feet everywhere and rattling his metaphorical chains in agony and despair.

Caelus can’t find it within himself to care anymore. No one presses the issue, which is fine by him. Let him mope it out of his system. He’ll be back to normal in a few days.

No one presses apart from Dan Heng, that is, because he’s Dan Heng.

“What happened to your head?” Dan Heng asks Caelus, cornering him in their room. His arms are crossed, and his frown is severe. He’s also unhelpfully positioned right in front of their door, so Caelus can’t even make a run for it—unless he tries to take a swan dive out of the window (which is looking incredibly tempting right now, even if Dan Heng would have a heart attack in the process).

“Don’t worry about it,” Caelus grunts instead.

He sounds petulant even to his own ears, and it makes Dan Heng only scrutinise him harder. Caelus shrinks away, feeling like a bug under a microscope.

Finally, Dan Heng sighs, and uncrosses his arms.

“Let’s go for a meal,” he suggests. “We haven’t eaten together in a while.”

His tone is so gentle that it kind of wants to make Caelus cry. He nods, and follows Dan Heng out of their chambers.

They end up at a restaurant in one of the back alleys of the city. Caelus hasn’t dined here before, but the place smells divine. The meat skewers sizzling on the counter nearly make Caelus’ mouth water, and he stares after them longingly.

“Two of the skewers, please,” Dan Heng tells the vendor smoothly.

His voice jolts Caelus out of his meat-induced reverie. “I was going to order for us,” he says, crestfallen.

Dan Heng raises a brow. “Would you have chosen differently?”

“... no.”

“Then my point stands.” You have to be faster than that, Dan Heng’s eyes say, glinting mischievously.

Caelus tries very hard not to pout at him, but then their food arrives, and he stops thinking about the events of the past few days.

He tears into his skewers. They’re divine; the meat is succulent and the vegetables are crisp. He nearly moans out loud, but just about restrains himself, because Dan Heng was kind enough to bring him here, and embarrassing him in return—while ordinarily would have been the funniest thing ever—is probably not the best way to pay him back.

Dan Heng also seems to be enjoying the meal. He’s eating at a much slower pace than Caelus, but he looks noticeably more relaxed. Happier, too.

Caelus swallows, his throat suddenly dry. He puts down his clean skewer.

Dan Heng looks satisfied enough that now would be a great time to ask him about Phainon and Mydei. Somehow, the thought of doing so makes Caelus’ side ache with quiet loneliness.

Under the table, Dan Heng gently nudges the side of Caelus’ foot with his own. “Credit for your thoughts?”

Caelus automatically nudges him back, but deliberately avoids his gaze. Depending on how this conversation goes, he’ll either need to take out his tissues, or his baseball bat. He doesn’t particularly want to use either.

“What?” he mumbles instead. “You know me. I’m not thinking about anything.”

Dan Heng also lays down his skewer. It’s half-finished, Caelus notes distantly.

“You seem… preoccupied,” Dan Heng says slowly. “Is everything all right?”

Caelus sighs. Well, Dan Heng’s given him an opportunity. It would be rude not to take it, after all.

“Listen. About you and Mydei …”

Predictably, Dan Heng tenses. “What about him?”

Caelus takes a deep breath. “Are you sure there’s nothing going on between you two?” he asks, trying not to sound too miserable.

Dan Heng gives him a wary look. “We only write,” he says, carefully, “Occasionally, and about nothing in particular.”

“You told me you needed ‘advice’. That’s not nothing,” Caelus presses.

Dan Heng stays silent, and Caelus has to fight the urge to twiddle his fingers or fidget or even crack another ill-timed joke, just to dispel the awkward air that’s suddenly grown between them like a persistent mold.

“Come onnnn,” Caelus chuckles awkwardly. Despite his best efforts, it comes out sounding incredibly forced. He winces. “You can tell me. We’re bros, aren’t we?”

For some reason, Dan Heng looks pained. Caelus also … actually feels pained after saying that, so he moves swiftly on.

“What about Phainon, then?” he asks instead.

At that, Dan Heng looks away and avoids Caelus’ gaze entirely. “Phainon and I… are simply engaging in a debate that has gone on for far longer than it should. I promise it’s not anything more than what it seems.”

“A debate?” Caelus wrinkles his nose. That’s not what he expected. “About what?”

“I’d rather not say,” Dan Heng says evasively.

Caelus valiantly tries not to feel hurt at that admission. He fails miserably.

“... Do you want me to talk to him?” Caelus hedges awkwardly.

At that, Dan Heng’s gaze snaps back to Caelus in an instant. His eyes are wide.

“No!” Dan Heng says, far too quickly. “No. It’s okay, truly.”

Caelus stares at him. Something’s off, because Dan Heng’s cheeks are pink, and they’re steadily growing pinker. So pink they could almost be mistaken for…

Oh, Caelus thinks wryly. That’s what it is.

He does need to get out the baseball bat after all—but not for Mydei.

Honestly, this should be a happy occasion. After all, even after his heartbreak on the Luofu, Dan Heng finally has a crush again. What a wonderful, beautiful thing.

Caelus tries to ignore the way his stomach falls at the prospect.

“Okay. I get it,” Caelus says, as brightly as he can manage. He barely manages to keep his voice from cracking.

Dan Heng visibly relaxes. He looks hopeful. “You do?”

“Yeah, of course,” Caelus says, braving a smile. He fiddles with the rim of his cup. “I just want you to be happy.”

At that, Dan Heng’s face softens. He reaches out, and pats the back of Caelus’ hand. His fingers are unfairly soft. “That’s sweet of you. But you don’t have to worry about me.”

But Caelus does have to worry. Dan Heng might be happy with his crush, but Caelus has to make sure that Dan Heng stays happy for the foreseeable future and beyond. He and March had promised that they would look out for him, after all, and since she’s down for the count, it’s up to Caelus to take up the mantle.

For all intents and purposes, Phainon is a taken man. But Caelus trusts his own memory; the conversations he’d overheard between Dan Heng and Phainon were definitely not just friendly. Is Phainon leading Dan Heng on? He has to know.

Phainon wouldn’t. He’s gentlemanly. And he loves Mydei, extremely non-platonically. So clearly the best case scenario here is that Phainon will very quickly (and gently) turn Dan Heng down, and then everyone can move on with their lives. Dan Heng might mope for a bit, but he should return to his usual self soon enough. At least, Caelus hopes so, because he has actually never seen Dan Heng in love before, so has no idea what it would look like. (He still thinks Dan Heng had something going on with Blade, but Dan Heng starts valiantly pretending he has hearing problems every time Caelus asks so what does he know).

Anyway. Given Phainon’s current affections for Mydei, Caelus figures that Dan Heng with a crush on Phainon can only mean a Dan Heng with his heart crushed. Which is fine—okay not fine, but salvageable —if Phainon lets him down gently.

If Phainon ever broke Dan Heng’s heart, Caelus would have to kill Phainon, and he doesn’t want that.

But at the same time, Caelus can’t deny that Dan Heng looks happy. Really happy. His cheeks are still as pink as a rose, but his frown lines look far less pronounced. His smile could probably stop a war right now. Or launch a thousand warships.

Could Phainon really look him in the eye and turn him down? Caelus probably couldn’t, and that’s saying something.

But the alternative is for Phainon to string Dan Heng along and never resolve anything between them, which Dan Heng would probably hate more.

Caelus decides that he won’t bring the issue up to Dan Heng now. Or ever, preferably. He’ll just sort it out himself.

That, however, is a problem for Future Caelus. Current Caelus decides to make the most of his dinner with his very good and very deserving friend, and finally changes the subject.

He flops dramatically against the table. “Did you know that Aglaea’s Garmentmakers apparently have a vendetta against me?”

“I didn’t,” Dan Heng hums. He leans forward, looking relieved at the change of topic, and pats the top of Caelus’ head. “Why do you think so?”

“Well…”

Future Caelus hates Past Caelus with a passion. Here he is, awake at an ungodly hour because he can’t stop thinking about Dan Heng’s doomed love life.

He still can’t believe that he was so wrong about Mydei. In one way, it works out better for everyone involved, because now all he potentially has to do is take his bat to Phainon. This still isn’t easy by any means of the word because Caelus has seen Phainon suplex beings twice his size, but it’s better than having to take his bat to Mydei.

Caelus doesn’t even know how he’d trek to Castrum Kremnos, let alone how he’d go and try to deliver a shovel talk to one of the most intimidating men he’s ever met. Mydei probably wouldn’t even move. He’d probably just cross his arms, look down at Caelus imposingly and raise an eyebrow in challenge, or something.

There’s also the black tide to think about, too. Mydei wouldn’t even have the time to listen to his shovel talk.

“Arghghhghghghghhhh,” Caelus whines.

“Go to sleep,” Dan Heng mumbles into his pillow.

Caelus cranes his neck and looks over to his companion. Dan Heng’s breathing is even, and his expression is unguarded. He looks completely at peace, and not at all like he dropped the world’s biggest bombshell on Caelus’ head yesterday.

“What am I going to do with you,” Caelus tells him despairingly.

Dan Heng’s response is to snore at him. Caelus waves a hand in front of his nose, and he doesn’t respond. Yep—he’s knocked out.

Hmm. Dan Heng is asleep, and one of his letters to Mydei is folded on the table next to him. If Caelus is careful enough, he can probably reach over Dan Heng’s sleeping form and swipe it.

No. He can’t be so nosy. Also, Dan Heng would realise what he’s done immediately. There’d be no saving himself from the disappointment afterwards.

Caelus gives the letter one last longing glance, before rolling over and burrowing under his blankets.

Who knows. Maybe he won’t even have to get out the bat. Maybe Dan Heng will get over his crush by himself, since he’s an honourable man, and Phainon and Mydei’s relationship will continue to blossom. That way, Caelus can whip out the tissues instead, and his bat can stay unused.

It would suck for Dan Heng, and would be really awkward if Phainon or Mydei ever found out, but hey, at least everyone’s friendships would remain intact.

Or maybe Phainon’s already done the opposite of letting Dan Heng down, and Dan Heng and Phainon are conducting a—secret relationship, instead. And Mydei’s just sending his approval in his letters. And Caelus has no idea about any of this, because Dan Heng’s too embarrassed to tell him.

No. Phainon and Mydei surely haven’t broken up. Their love story was the stuff of ages. Everyone in the city was rooting for them. They even made Caelus the third wheel of this planet.

But then again, Caelus remembers the way one disgruntled woman in Penacony complained to him about how long-distance relationships never worked out… and if Dan Heng really has met the love of his life here, then who is Caelus to stop him?

With that delightful thought in mind, Caelus resentfully drifts off to sleep.

Caelus lied. He needs his bat immediately.

Phainon is growing tenser with each day that passes. His smile doesn’t quite reach his eyes anymore, and Caelus has no idea what happened to make him so anxious. The only information he gets are snippets of conversation, none of which are directed towards him.

“Have you heard from Mydei?” Caelus overhears Phainon ask Dan Heng. He sounds strained. “I know he’s been writing to you—”

“—I’m sorry,” Dan Heng says, sounding truly apologetic.

“—just that, I haven’t heard from him in a while—”

Phainon sounds wretched. Caelus has never heard him this close to falling apart before—

—which is when he realises—

Oh. Phainon and Mydei are definitely still together. And there’s no way that Phainon is leading Dan Heng on.

But that doesn’t make sense, because Caelus saw Dan Heng with another letter yesterday, which surely Dan Heng would’ve brought up by now, knowing that Phainon is worried out of his mind? Unless—

Caelus stops dead in his tracks. Unless…

He thinks back. Counts in his head the number of letters he’d seen Dan Heng receive, and the length of time between each. He compares them against the number of times he’d caught Phainon and Dan Heng having their ‘discussions’—or were they even discussions? Had Phainon been asking Dan Heng about Mydei, instead?

It doesn’t make sense. Mydei would never—cheat, he’s too respectable and honest but—what if the black tide has—Caelus has no idea. Side effects that cause infidelity? No—even in the black tide Mydei would stay faithful. He’d say something like “I may die but my feelings will never die” blah blah blah.

Caelus frowns. It doesn’t make sense.

When Phainon starts looking like he’s close to fraying apart at the seams, Caelus decides to take matters into his own hands. He helped undoom this yaoi—there’s no way he’s seeing it get doomed again.

He marches outside.

“Mydei,” Caelus hisses to the sky. “Hey, Mydei—you aren’t being accidentally rizzed up by Dan Heng too, are you? I know he’s alluring and sexy and hot but you have to resist it! He has too many victims! Trust me, you have to ignore him!”

No response. It seems that the boyfriend privileges don’t extend to him. Defeated, Caelus trudges back to his room.

It must be accidental. That was how Dan Heng picked up Boothill, too. There’s no way Dan Heng could have picked up Mydei on purpose.

Caelus feels like tearing his hair out. He doesn’t want Dan Heng to pick up anyone. What the hell do you call that? Seriously, why does he want to swing a bat at anyone approaching Dan Heng with nefarious intentions? Is Dan Heng just that—easy to protect?

He’s the Express Guard. He can take care of himself perfectly well. But Caelus’ mind refuses to compute.

Is Dan Heng pursuing Mydei, or is he pursuing Phainon? Or are either of them pursuing him? Is Dan Heng the problem? Why does it feel like there’s equal evidence for both scenarios?

Caelus freezes.

Oh shit, he thinks, with startling clarity.

Are Mydei and Phainon fighting over Dan Heng? Or are they all… a throuple?

Surely not.

Surely not???

Phainon disappears from Okhema. Dan Heng holes himself up in his room. Caelus, for his part, panics.

Is it simply Dan Heng’s destiny to become entangled in doomed threesomes? It would be fine (no it would not) if they were all in a happy throuple. But Caelus swears he saw Phainon near tears before he left, and found Dan Heng with his head in his hands right after. They didn’t look happy at all.

So this is either some doomed yaoi to doomed polyamory yaoi pipeline (polyaoi?) or it’s some sort of doomed love triangle, and Caelus can’t figure out what’s worse, and he wishes, above everything, that Dan Heng would trust him enough to tell him.

Therefore, he thinks it makes sense for him to be a bit irrational after running around in circles trying to get to the bottom of everything. So what comes next is—fine, he admits that it’s wrong, but he spent so long trying to get Mydei and Phainon together, and Dan Heng was actually helping him by the end of it, and even if Dan Heng, Phainon and Mydei are actually a thing then Caelus would get over it and be happy for them but clearly none of them are happy, so what the hell is going on?

Tribbie only laughs at him when he tries to ask. Caelus is left with no one to turn to, and Dan Heng’s destroyed his whiteboard, so he only really has one option left.

He yanks Dan Heng behind a wall.

“DAN HENG. I CAN’T BELIEVE YOU.”

“Caelus?” Dan Heng hisses, alarmed. “What’s going on—”

“DOES THE SANCTITY OF MARRIAGE MEAN NOTHING TO YOU ANYMORE,” Caelus keeps bellowing. “YOU CAN’T JUST COME TO EVERY PLANET AND EXPECT A NEW HUSBAND—LET ALONE TWO—LIKE SOME SORT OF—CURIO DISPENSER FOR WIDOWERS.”

Dan Heng’s face goes through a peculiar series of expressions: shock, confusion, anger—and then he just looks embarrassed.

“Can you just—” Dan Heng puts his head in his hands. “Please stop shouting.”

Caelus thinks of Phainon and Dan Heng, or Mydei and Dan Heng, or maybe Phainon, Mydei and Dan Heng, and wonders whether maybe he’ll turn his back on them one day and they’ll be having a threesome without telling him. Objectively, there’s nothing wrong with that, but it also kind of makes Caelus want to set Amphoreus on fire, or more specifically set Phainon and Mydei on fire, because he would never do that to Dan Heng, but at the same time Caelus quite literally lost hair over getting Phainon and Mydei together, and honestly they’re probably fireproof anyway, because one of them is literally a demigod, and the other one is the human equivalent of a tank and missile rolled in one, so he’d have to try something else, but then Tribbie would be sad, and—he may be doomposting, here, but can you blame him?

“I EXPECTED BETTER FROM YOU,” Caelus howls. “AFTER I WORKED SO HARD TO GET THEM TOGETHER—”

Dan Heng doesn’t speak to him after that. Tribbie keeps looking between them with worried glances, but gives them a wide berth.

Caelus hates the silence, but he doesn’t want to back down. He’s no closer to finding out anything. And if Dan Heng doesn’t want to tell him, then he’s not going to beg.

Eventually, he decides to take up one of the citizens’ requests, just to clear his mind. He doesn’t take Dan Heng with him. It’s a simple request, anyway—one of the shopkeepers is just asking him to get rid of some Titankin for them, which shouldn’t be too much trouble.

Until he realises that the shopkeeper severely underestimated just how many Titankin were camping out in this patch of the road, and that Caelus was so desperate to get out of the city that he forgot to pack anything that could heal him. Soon enough, Caelus is laid out flat on his back, and a Titankin is looming over him. It’s quite possibly the shittiest way to die, and in his last moments, Caelus curses himself for being so stupid.

Somewhere in the distance, a voice calls his name. Caelus can’t pinpoint whether it’s real, or a hallucination. The blood loss kind of makes it difficult to tell.

He promptly passes out.

Miraculously, Caelus wakes up.

“Hey,” he coughs, weakly. His eyelids are stuck shut together, so he has to grope around until his hand hits something solid. “Why’s it so… wet…”

“Caelus!” a voice shouts, far too loud and panicked to be comfortable.

Caelus groans. His ears are ringing, and he feels like he got run over like one of Penacony’s insane drivers. “Not so loud…”

The stickiness in his eyes slowly subsides. He cracks his eyes open, and watches blearily as the figure hovering above him swims into view.

“How do you feel?” Dan Heng asks.

“Like shit,” Caelus moans. He tries to sit up, but his head feels like someone dunked it in molasses and left it there to rot. He ends up flopping ungracefully back into Dan Heng’s arms. “... What happened?”

Dan Heng shifts so that Caelus isn’t half collapsed on the floor, and manoeuvres him so that he’s snug against Dan Heng’s chest.

“You were caught in an ambush,” Dan Heng tells him. His voice is tight. “What were you thinking?”

Caelus blinks. Why is Dan Heng hissing at him? Silly lizard.

“I was thinking,” he manages slowly, because words are suddenly difficult right now, “that I could help.”

“And how did that turn out?”

Caelus blinks at him incredulously. Dan Heng only glares back.

“Are you—mad at me?”

“What do you think,” Dan Heng seethes. Caelus nearly recoils; he’s never seen Dan Heng look this intense before. His gaze looks like it could burn through glass.  “Why were you out here alone?”

“Why wouldn’t I be? Someone asked me to help them, so I did,” Caelus points out. “Besides, you’re literally cuddling me. And it’s raining. You’re making it rain.”

“That’s besides the point!” Dan Heng erupts, still cuddling him.

“And I’m—stop it, I’m supposed to be mad at you,” Caelus says, outraged. He tries to shake out of Dan Heng’s grip, but Dan Heng, the cheater, only wraps his arms around him tighter. “You—you homewrecker!”

Silence. Dan Heng continues to stare at him, but his face slackens in surprise.

Caelus glares back, defiant. He hasn’t said anything wrong.

“Don’t worry. He hasn’t wrecked any homes—” Phainon pipes up from Caelus’ other side, and Caelus nearly scrambles out of Dan Heng’s arms because since when did they have an audience? “—or any other structures, for that matter. To be honest, it’s nice to have some rain in the city for once.”

When the hell did Phainon get here? Caelus thinks woozily, before: What the hell is he talking about?

“... Did I say something wrong?” Phainion asks, after a moment of silence.

Right. They don’t have homewreckers in Amphoreus. They probably have—harlots, or something. But Dan Heng the Harlot just doesn’t have the same ring to it as Dan Heng the Homewrecker.

Dan Heng shakes himself out of his stupor. He rounds on Caelus again.

“What are you talking about?” he asks. And he has the audacity to look exasperated! Caelus bristles with indignation. “Who are you talking about?”

“You know exactly what I’m talking about,” Caelus accuses. “I know you’re like—the hottest man ever, and you’re a total catch, but you can’t just go around—” here, he lowers his voice, “—breaking up other couples!”

Phainon is giving them an odd look. Caelus ignores him, and struggles to get up. He gives Dan Heng a look of profound sadness.

“I didn’t go through my ten step plan for nothing,” Caelus says in a small voice. “And now look at what's happened. Mydei’s in love with you.”

Phainon inhales sharply. “Mydei’s what?”

“And Phainon’s in love with you too!”

This makes Phainon pause. “... I am?”

At last, the cat’s out of the bag. Dully, Caelus realises that he can finally come clean with his deductions.

“You don’t have to deny it,” Caelus says miserably. “I overheard you both. I saw the letters, too. And I don’t blame you either.” Here, he turns to Phainon apologetically. “Dan Heng’s just like that. He attracts everyone he meets. I thought you two would be excluded, but… “

Dan Heng simply gapes at him. For the first time in Caelus’ life, Dan Heng actually looks shellshocked. He’d be scrabbling to take a photo, if the situation weren’t so severe.

Then, Dan Heng sighs. He leans forward, looking suddenly intent.

“Caelus,” he says calmly. He presses the back of his hand against Caelus’ forehead. The coolness of his touch feels like a soothing balm. “You’re delirious. You need a healer—”

“No! Listen,” Caelus protests, batting away Dan Heng’s hand. “They’re—Phainon and Mydei —they’re made for each other. And I know you’d never do this, so I thought that maybe you’re just doing this accidentally again—but then you talked about the letters, and I overheard you the other day, and—Dan Heng, this isn’t like you!” Caelus draws back. He looks Dan Heng in the eye. “What’s going on?”

“... Alright. To clarify, and just so that I know that I’m correct in my thinking,” Dan Heng says, sounding strangely like he’s speaking through gritted teeth. “You believe… that both Mydei and Phainon are—in love with me. Is that correct?”

“And you like them back,” Caelus says miserably, feeling the admission cut through him like a butter knife and he’s the poor slab of butter. “Obviously. But you can’t just—have one of them and not tell the other, because they’re still together!”

Another silence follows. Crickets chirp in the background. The rain continues to fall, occasional droplets splashing onto Caelus’ soggy hair.

On his left, Phainon coughs. He opens his mouth, raises his hand like he wants to speak, and then lowers his hand just as hesitantly.

“I can’t in good conscience let this happen,” Caelus admits, feeling small. “I had to intervene, somehow.”

He stares determinedly at the ground. He hopes it swallows him whole.

“You think I have feelings for Phainon,” Dan Heng asks him, flatly, (“Hey,” Phainon protests weakly in the background) “and Mydei?”

“... and probably all the other men that you’ve picked up?” Caelus says, looking up again. Dan Heng is still staring at him, utterly expressionless. “So I thought it wasn’t a foregone conclusion.”

Dan Heng continues to stare at him, unblinking. Caelus stares back with the saddest gaze he can muster, until he really can’t hold it anymore.

He coughs. “... I feel like I’m missing something.”

“Hm,” says Dan Heng. He tips his head back to gaze at the sky, looking contemplative. He also looks kind of pained.

“Are my affections really that unknown?” Dan Heng says finally.

“What affections?” Caelus asks, feeling incredibly lost.

Dan Heng doesn’t say a word, but his cheeks are steadily growing pinker.

Caelus tries again. “What affections? Dan Heng?”

“Caelus, please,” Dan Heng groans. Phainon, having wandered a ways away for some reason, erupts into a suspicious coughing fit.

Caelus sits back, and really thinks about it. If Dan Heng’s adamant that his affections aren’t for Phainon, and they aren’t for Mydei, then who else could they be for? It’s not as if there’s… anyone else…

He glances at Dan Heng. Dan Heng, who is still holding his gaze, even though his cheeks are flushing a furious red. His hand is still steady on Caelus’ shoulder. Caelus thinks about how worried Dan Heng had been just now, and how embarrassed he was in all those moments they were alone together, and…

… ah.

“Oh,” Caelus says weakly. “... I may be an idiot?”

At that, Phainon lets out a cheer, and claps gleefully behind them. Like some sort of… giant seal, Caelus thinks deliriously. And Dan Heng… Dan Heng just closes his eyes momentarily, and exhales, before opening them again, looking more determined than ever.

“Do you understand now?” Dan Heng asks him, intently.

Caelus gives him a wobbly smile. His head is swimming, but the sour feeling in his gut has evaporated.

Dan Heng has affections for him? This entire time?

Caelus raises his hand, and gives him a wobbly thumbs up. He doesn’t get to see Dan Heng’s reaction, because black spots start to dance across his vision. That can’t be good, Caelus thinks, too slowly.

“I’mgoingtopassout,” he slurs, before he passes out.

When Caelus wakes up again, he feels infinitely better than he did the last time woke up. Partly because he’s waking up in an actual bed with clean sheets, and partly because Dan Heng’s holding his hand at his bedside.

“You’re great at worrying me,” Dan Heng tells him unhappily.

Caelus looks at him. He’s still in his rumpled clothes. The sight fills Caelus with fondness. Did Dan Heng stay here the entire time?

“You love me,” Caelus grins. He squeezes Dan Heng’s hand. “That’s so embarrassing for you.”

Before Dan Heng can retort, another voice comes from the door, sounding equally as exasperated.

“Thank Kephale,” Phainon sighs. He’s leaning against the doorframe, looking as sprightly as ever. “I can finally leave.”

Caelus yelps, nearly sending Dan Heng flying. Dan Heng gives him an unimpressed look.

“What are you doing here?” Caelus asks.

“I wanted to make sure you were alright. But also, knowing your track record, I could hardly leave before I heard those words coming from your mouth,” Phainon explains, before he grimaces. “If Mydei and I were anything like you two, then I owe you an apology for what we put you through.”

He looks so sincere that Caelus is half afraid that he’s going to bow to them.

“It’s no big deal,” he hurries. “Thanks for—uh, making sure. Sorry it took so long?”

Phainon only smiles at him. “No apologies needed. But I still haven’t offered my congratulations! I’m glad things worked out for you both.” Then, he grins wider. “May I ask —did we help, at all?”

For a moment, Caelus is confused. Help with what?

“Dan Heng?” Phainon prods, looking like he's barely suppressing a laugh.

“Please remind me to never take both of your advice ever again,” Dan Heng sighs. “Especially after you made it into a competition.”

Slowly, the gears begin to turn in Caelus’ head. When they click, it feels like someone pulled the bed out from under him and sent him crashing to the floor.

He points an accusing finger at Phainon, and then at Dan Heng, and then in the general direction of the sky.

“I thought you three were in a polyamorous relationship,” he shrieks.

“Yes, you told us,” Phainon chuckles, amused.

Caelus feels like his eyes are bugging out of their skull. He whips around to face Dan Heng. “But you—you kept going to Phainon—”

“Truthfully, that misconception was my fault. I was roping him into my schemes,” Phainon admits. “Sorry, Dan Heng.”

Dan Heng nods. “Apology accepted.”

“and Dan Heng, you—” Caelus sputters. How are these two so calm?! “You kept getting letters even after Phainon didn’t—”

Dan Heng sighs. “No. I was rereading them. You just happened to catch me in the act.” He looks pointedly at Phainon. “Mydei gives good advice.”

“But—but—” Caelus sputters, again. He thinks back to the reams of letters that Dan Heng kept receiving. None of this adds up, but— “Then how many letters did you get?”

Dan Heng leans back in his chair. “A grand total of two,” he says drily. “Far from the dozens you believed I was receiving. Behind Phainon’s back, even.”

“Hyacine laughed for hours when she heard,” Phainon tells him, eyes twinkling. “I think it really made her day.”

Caelus can’t believe any of this. “But—!”

“I was asking for advice,” Dan Heng emphasises. “Homewrecking? Do you really think so little of me? Honestly.”

“You can’t blame me!” Caelus screeches. “I thought you kept sneaking off to write letters, and you were always around Phainon, and Phainon was upset—”

“Don’t worry. That’s been resolved,” Phainon pipes up. “Mydei sends his regards.”

Caelus’ mouth is hanging open. He’s probably gaping like a fish. He feels a little stupid. Scratch that—a lot stupid.

“So it really was—nothing?” he says, dumbfounded. “You didn’t have a crush on either of them, Dan Heng?”

Dan Heng sighs, eternally long-suffering. “No, Caelus, I didn’t.”

“The first time we met, Dan Heng tried to skewer me with Cloud Piercer, because I dared lay a hand on your shoulder,” Phainon laughs. “Considering how perceptive you were to my own feelings, I’m surprised you never realised your own.”

Dan Heng closes his eyes. “Sometimes I fear that his perceptiveness is selective.”

“Hey,” Caelus says weakly.

Phainon claps his hands together. “Well! I’m glad that’s settled,” he says brightly. “I’ll leave you two to catch up.”

He leaves with a wave. Caelus waits for the door to shut behind him, before turning to Dan Heng.

“We’re talking about this,” he demands.

“You brought most of this upon yourself,” Dan Heng reminds him. He reaches out, and brushes the hair from Caelus’ forehead. Caelus won’t deny that the gesture makes his heart flutter a little bit. “But I’m happy to speak about this later. For now, you should rest.”

“Fine. Since my wonderful doctor so kindly insists.” Caelus tries to blow him a kiss, but it’s hard to do so with one free hand and rapidly approaching fatigue.

Dan Heng’s expression softens, and Caelus fights the urge to grin. It’s nice to know he was the one putting those expressions on there, and not their friends. Which—whoops, he’ll have to apologise to both Mydei and Phainon after this.

He does have one last burning question, though. He sits up, looks Dan Heng directly in the eye, and fights to keep his face neutral.

“... Did you really soak all of Okhema?”

Dan Heng’s face quickly switches from fond to exasperated. “I’ll soak you,” he threatens.

He squeezes Caelus’ hand anyway, so Caelus counts that as a solid win.

No doomed yaoi for anyone today, he thinks to himself happily. And hopefully not on the next planet, either…
